title: Page with Multiple Heading Levels

illustrates.quote: Print books use various methods to distinguish headings: different fonts and font sizes, color, placement on the page, etc. Just as print headings provide a hierarchy structure of levels, an effort should be made to achieve the same type of structure in braille. This is done after a careful examination of headings in the table of contents and the body of text. It is important to be consistent in the treatment of similar print headings throughout the entire transcription. (See Sample 4-1: Page with Multiple Heading Levels on page 4-14.)

print.notes: This is the print page Formats uses to show a real page with many simultaneous heading levels together: a section-number banner, a page title, a sidebar box with its own title and cell-5 sub-headings, a 'Main Idea' tab, and a cell-7 callout, followed on the second braille page by a centered section heading and two levels of run-in headings -- exercising centered/cell-5/cell-7 and paragraph-heading treatment side by side, illustrating rule 4.1.1's call for a consistent braille heading hierarchy. The braille excerpt does not reproduce every sidebar bullet or vocabulary-list entry in full -- only enough of each to show its heading treatment, using the '444' continuation marker where print's own list is longer than the excerpt transcribes.
print.surroundingText: Cross-referenced from rule 4.1.1 (examine the table of contents and body to establish a consistent heading hierarchy); also relevant to rule 4.2.1 (extending centered headings to more than one level when there are more than three distinct print heading levels), though 4.2.1's own explicit cross-reference is to Example 4-1, not this sample.
print.printFeatures: A two-column textbook page: a narrow tan sidebar (Reading Preview box) at left, a wide main column at right; heavy use of color-coded banners and labels to distinguish print heading levels, continuing onto a second print page for "Real-World Reading Link" and "Nonspecific Immunity" with their own run-in sub-headings.

pageBreaks.note: The source's own line numbering silently restarts at 1 after line 25 (no explicit '—New Braille Page—' marker text): the boundary between the two braille pages transcribed for this one print page (printed page 4-15/PDF p.119 and printed page 4-16/PDF p.120). A coded running-head token at the end of line 1 of each half ('#ajhd' = 1084 on the first half, 'a#ajhd' = 1084a on the second) confirms both carry the same original textbook page number 1084 (matching the print image's own '1084' page footer).

braille.notes: Two braille pages. Page 1 (lines 1-25): line 1 the centered heading 'Section 37.2' plus a running-head page-number code at the right margin; line 2 centered 'The Immune System'; line 4 centered 'Reading Preview'; line 6 cell-5 'Objectives' + line 7-9 its abbreviated list item, ending '444'; line 11 cell-5 'Review Vocabulary' + lines 12-15 its definition entry; line 17 cell-5 'New Vocabulary' + lines 18-20 its first entry, ending '444'; line 22 cell-5 'MAIN Idea' + lines 23-24 its lead sentence, with a trailing reference-mark code at the end of line 25. Page 2 (lines 26-48, source renumbers 1-23): line 26 the cell-7 heading 'Real-World Reading Link' (6 leading blank cells, NOT centered) plus its own running-head code; lines 27-28 its paragraph; line 30 the centered heading 'Nonspecific Immunity'; lines 32-36 its two paragraphs; line 38 the cell-5 heading 'Barriers'; lines 39-40 its paragraph; lines 42-44 the paragraph opening with the inline run-in heading 'Skin barrier' (bold typeform, not relocated); lines 46-48 likewise for 'Chemical barriers'.

uncertain: Whether 'Section 37.2' and 'Reading Preview' are properly rule-4.2 'centered headings', or are running-head/box-title material that merely happens to sit at a centered indent, was judged from the braille's own indent arithmetic (indent matches (40-length)/2 for both, exactly) rather than from an explicit statement in the rule text that a section-number banner or box title counts as a 'heading' for hierarchy purposes.

Print's full 'Objectives' (3 bullets), 'New Vocabulary' (9 terms) and 'Review Vocabulary' lists are given here in full (matching the print image, PDF p.118) even though the actual braille excerpt transcribes only the first item of each and replaces the rest with a '444' continuation marker; this print.blocks/braille divergence has no representation in this section's print-block schema (there is no 'more items omitted' block kind), so gold-run.mjs is expected to report a documented line-count mismatch here, not a bug.

Several right-margin coded tokens (e.g. line 1's '#ajhd', line 25's trailing reference mark, page-2 line 1's 'a#ajhd') are read as running-head/page-number/reference codes by their numeric form and position, not verified against a full braille transcriber's-code reference.
resolution: braille.lines agree byte-for-byte between runs (independently re-checked). print.blocks structure was substantially rebuilt from the PDF page image (p.118) directly, since the two runs disagreed extensively on block order/kind/level (84 raw diffs): run A omitted "Reading Preview" as a separate block (folding it into descriptive text) even though the braille gives it its own centered line; run B, conversely, is missing several blocks A has and mis-orders/mis-levels others. The image (references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf, p.118) was read directly to rebuild the full, correctly-ordered block list, and every heading's level was independently verified against the (agreed) braille.lines' own leading-blank-cell counts (see differences.md for the line-by-line indent table). `illustrates.rule` resolved to "4.1.1" only (run A), not run B's "4.1.1 / 4.2.1": rule 4.1.1's own text is what explicitly cross-references "Sample 4-1" (line ~3143 of the .txt); rule 4.2.1 cross-references Example 4-1 instead, and the §11 precedent's illustrates schema names one specific rule.
